title: 3D Maze with Real-Time Pathfinding and Wall Collision
prompt:
Create a 3D maze game with real-time pathfinding visualization, player movement with wall collision detection, and a minimap using Three.js. Apply wall textures from loaded images. The entire application must be in a single HTML file.

## Three.js Import
Use this importmap in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';

## Scene Setup
- Background 0x111122.
- PerspectiveCamera as first-person view, height y=1.5, FOV 70.
- No OrbitControls — this is first-person.
- Ambient light (0x334455, intensity 0.3) for dark atmosphere.
- A point light attached to the player position (0xffaa44, intensity 1.5, distance 10) — flashlight effect.
- An additional distant directional light (0x223355, intensity 0.2) from above.

## Maze Generation
- Use recursive backtracker (DFS) to generate a 15x15 maze on the XZ plane.
- Each cell is 3x3 units. Total maze: 45x45 units.
- Walls: box geometry (3 wide, 3 tall, 0.3 thick), textured with 'brick_diffuse.jpg' (repeat 1x1 per wall segment).
- Floor: plane at y=0, size 45x45, dark color 0x333344.
- Ceiling: plane at y=3, size 45x45, color 0x222233.
- Start position: cell (0, 0) — bottom-left corner.
- Exit position: cell (14, 14) — top-right corner, marked with a glowing green pillar.

## Player Movement & Collision
- WASD for movement: W=forward, S=backward, A=strafe left, D=strafe right.
- Mouse controls camera look direction (pointer lock on click).
- Player speed: 5 units/sec.
- **Wall collision**: use AABB collision. Player has a collision capsule (radius 0.3). Before moving, check if new position would overlap any wall. If so, slide along the wall (separate X and Z components and test independently).
- Smooth movement with delta-time.

## Pathfinding Visualization
- Press 'P' to toggle pathfinding overlay: compute A* path from player's current cell to the exit.
- Visualize the path as glowing green cubes (0.3x0.1x0.3) on the floor at each path cell.
- Path updates every 0.5 seconds as the player moves.
- Show explored cells (closed set) as dim blue floor markers.

## Minimap
- Render a minimap in the top-right corner (canvas overlay, 200x200 pixels).
- Draw maze walls as white lines, player as a green dot with direction indicator, exit as a red dot.
- Minimap shows the full maze layout.

## Controls
- WASD: movement.
- Mouse: look direction.
- Click canvas: pointer lock.
- Press 'P': toggle pathfinding overlay.
- Press 'M': toggle minimap.
- Press 'R': reset player to start.
- Press 'N': generate new maze.

## HUD (id='hud')
- Player cell (id='hud-cell'): current grid cell 'x,y'
- Path length (id='hud-path'): A* path length to exit in cells
- Distance to exit (id='hud-dist'): Euclidean distance, 1 decimal
- Time (id='hud-time'): seconds since start, 1 decimal
- Status (id='hud-status'): 'Playing' / 'Won!'
- Maze size (id='hud-size'): '15x15'

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
- `playerCell`: {x, y}
- `pathLength`: number
- `distToExit`: number (rounded to 2 decimals)
- `elapsedTime`: number (rounded to 1 decimal)
- `status`: string ('Playing'|'Won!')
- `mazeSize`: number (always 15)
- `pathfindingEnabled`: boolean
- `minimapEnabled`: boolean
- `frameCount`: number
- `playerValid`: boolean (no NaN in player position)
- `wallCollisions`: number (total wall collision events)

Ensure the animation loop updates __3D_STATE__ every frame before rendering.
physics_constraints: Player must not pass through walls (AABB collision). Maze must be solvable (DFS guarantees connectivity). A* path must find shortest path. Player moves in 3D first-person. Distance to exit must decrease along optimal path. Win condition: player reaches exit cell. No NaN in player position.
